nodes.label: ISO/TS 19144-3:2024 Land Use Meta Language (LUML)
nodes.author: ISO/TC 211; FAO; CEN/TC 287
nodes.rationale: Standardizing the multitude of national Land Use classifications is not meaningful; a metalanguage that lets systems be described, compared and translated without replacing them is. Content on Land Use was moved out of ISO 19144-2:2012 into this new part, and registration was split into a separate part to generalize it for Land Cover, Land Use and future parts.

nodes.label: Land Use
nodes.rationale: Defined as arrangements, activities and inputs people undertake in a certain Land Cover type to maintain it or produce change. Defined in terms of human activities over periods of time, so that a direct link to Land Cover can be established while keeping the two concepts separate.

nodes.label: Land Cover
nodes.rationale: Defined in ISO 19144-2 as the (bio)physical cover; considered the visible result of some aspects of Land Use at a moment in time, hence kept as a separate concept from Land Use.

nodes.label: Land Use Meta Language (LUML)
nodes.rationale: Any set of basic elements could form a metalanguage, but to compare and integrate data from different Land Use systems one metalanguage must be standardized. Its structure deliberately matches ISO 19144-2 so Land Cover and Land Use classes can be used together to describe complex cases.

nodes.label: Land Cover Land Use functional link
nodes.rationale: It is not efficient to create independent Land Cover and Land Use systems and later build an artificial connection; historical hybrid ontologies where terms are interchangeable cannot explain complex relationships. A framework that dynamically integrates both, modelled through functional, temporal and duration relationship types, is preferred.

nodes.label: Land Characterization (combined Land Cover Land Use)
nodes.rationale: Adding a few attributes from one schema to the other (Description Types 1 and 2 augmented) is only a special case and should be used sparingly; a proper combination requires a combined Land Characterization ontology.

nodes.label: Land Use function
nodes.rationale: Function = the specific purpose a piece of land serves and the output it provides. Subdivision into functions and activities provides structure; without it there would be a very large number of single Land Use entities.

nodes.label: Land Use activity
nodes.rationale: Activities = what actually takes place in physical or observable terms on the land under a specific function; complementary to functions.

nodes.label: Five main Land Use functions
nodes.rationale: production, provision, residential, regulative, insubstantial other; list extensible by registration of additional functional elements.

nodes.label: Triadic relationship Land Objects / Land Events / Land Functions
nodes.rationale: Observing the land from an integrated perspective highlights a strong triadic relationship between (bio)physical objects, time-bounded events and socio-economic functions.

nodes.label: Design paradigm: simple, stable, comprehensive, scientifically sound
nodes.rationale: The integrated framework should be simple (most logical diagnostic criteria), stable (universal long-term criteria), comprehensive (all aspects of LC and LU) and scientifically sound (tied to natural vegetation and human activity definitions).

nodes.label: Three semantic levels: legend, classification system, metalanguage
nodes.rationale: A legend is concrete (instances exist in a geographic area); a classification system is one level above and defines descriptive criteria for possible classes; the metalanguage is one level higher and provides the structure to describe classification systems.

nodes.label: <<metalanguage>> stereotype
nodes.rationale: Applied to a class whose instances are other classes that are described by the metalanguage class; marks metamodel-level objects distinct from Application Schema level classes.

nodes.label: Ambiguity of the term class (UML vs classification)
nodes.rationale: UML 'class' and classification 'class' conflict unavoidably; adjectives (UML class, classification class, legend class) are used where possible. Same for attribute, object, element, component, characteristic.

nodes.label: ISO/TC 211 two-letter class prefix convention (LU, LC, CL, EL, CV)
nodes.rationale: Prefix identifies the standard and package defining a UML class, giving a globally unique name. Classes defined in this document use 'LU'.

nodes.label: Object-based ontology (UML model based) approach
nodes.rationale: No fixed list of categories; unlimited combinations of well-defined attributes; each Land Feature class characterized by a UML model; flexible for scientific advance and XML/XSD instantiation; same object-oriented logic as LCML makes modelling the LC-LU functional relationship straightforward.

nodes.label: Building block approach to class description
nodes.rationale: Detailed elements are defined which can be combined to create a precise description of any Land Cover or Land Use class (ISO 19144-2:2023, 8.1).

nodes.label: Registration of code lists, characteristics and classification systems
nodes.rationale: Some characteristics and code lists must be registered; registration was separated from ISO 19144-2:2012 into another part of the series to generalize it across Land Use, Land Cover and future parts and to address implementation issues.

nodes.label: XML Schema as metaschema vs Application Schema
nodes.rationale: An XML expression of this document is a metaschema; actual LC/LU data encoding must be at the Application Schema level one instantiation lower, so XSD generation is an implementation issue not addressed here.

LC_HorizontalPattern (ISO 19144-2)
nodes.rationale: A horizontal pattern can represent a complex Land Cover object composed of two or more distinct Land Cover features handled as a unicum.

nodes.label: LU_LandCoverLandUseRelationship
nodes.rationale: Collection class composing LU_FunctionalElementArrangement with LC_HorizontalPattern; attributes functionalElementRelationship, temporalRelationship, duration (alias timeLength) and durationUom (alias timeLengthUom, default months).

nodes.label: LU_FunctionsElementArrangement (LU_FunctionalElementArrangement)
nodes.rationale: Attributes: functionalRelationship (default primary), temporalRelationship, relevance (percentage), endProductsValue (registered product classification), chronologicalStatus. Composed of LU_LandUseFunctionElement and LU_ActivitiesArrangement.

nodes.label: LU_ActivitiesArrangement
nodes.rationale: Attributes: functionalRelationship, temporalRelationship, activityRelevance (1-100 %), orderSequence (CharacterString, e.g. seeding before harvesting), activitiesComposition.

nodes.label: LU_RelationshipType code list (primary, dominant, secondary, limited)
LU_Residential
nodes.rationale: Attributes type (LU_ResidentialTypes) and intensityValue (positive real; unit of measure to be established).

nodes.label: LU_Regulative
nodes.rationale: Regulation is only briefly addressed to provide a link to an external specification; detailed rights, restrictions, responsibilities and parties may be described per the LADM in ISO 19152-1.

nodes.label: LU_PlantAgriculture
nodes.rationale: Attributes exploitationType, intensity, scale.

nodes.label: LU_AnimalFarming
nodes.rationale: Attributes type, species, intensity, productionSystem; several LU_Production classes may be aggregated, e.g. beef and dairy cattle in mixed farming.

nodes.label: LU_HardMaterialExtraction
nodes.rationale: Attributes position, miningTypes, materialTypes.

nodes.label: LU_OilGasExtraction
nodes.rationale: Attributes extractedMaterialTypes, extractionTypes.

nodes.label: LU_IntensityTypes code list
nodes.rationale: Defined through registration; intensity may be output-oriented (yield per area/input) or input-oriented (input costs over usable area).

nodes.label: LU_FarmScaleRelatedTypes (largeScale, mediumScale, smallScale)
nodes.rationale: Major discriminant is type of labour supply.

LU_UtilitiesTypes (waterAndSewageTreatment, pipelines, wasteTreatment, electricityDistribution, gasAndThermalPowerDistribution, otherUtilities)
Land Use Meta Language (LUML)
nodes.rationale: A fixed, stable vocabulary of metalanguage elements is needed so descriptions of different Land Use classification systems remain comparable.

nodes.label: Land Use activity
nodes.rationale: Activities are correlated to functions through the activity arrangement structure so that what people do on land is modelled separately from the purpose (function).

nodes.label: ISO 19144-4 Registration and Implementation Aspects (under preparation)
LU_Regulative
nodes.rationale: Detailed rights, restrictions, responsibilities and parties for a Regulative function are delegated to an external LADM (ISO 19152-1) document rather than modelled in LUML.

nodes.label: LU_Activities (abstract)
nodes.rationale: Eight abstract subtypes each correspond to a function type, so every activity is anchored to the function it serves; all subtypes inherit the eight operation attributes.

nodes.label: Activity arrangement structure
nodes.rationale: Four relationship types (functional, temporal, relevance, order sequence) are needed because activities within a function group can dominate, coexist, cycle, or follow each other; significance is context dependent so relevance is a percentage.

nodes.label: LU_OperationTypeList code list
nodes.rationale: Left to be defined through registration so that operation vocabularies can be tailored nationally without changing the metalanguage.

nodes.label: LU_LandUseFunctionalElement
nodes.rationale: Its subtypes (the basic metalanguage elements) may only be changed by amendment of the standard, giving a route to extend the language that is well controlled by the standardization process.

nodes.label: LUML extension process
nodes.rationale: The metalanguage vocabulary must be stable for descriptions of different classification systems to be comparable; hence core elements change only by amendment while activities and code lists extend by registration.

nodes.label: Registration of extensions
nodes.rationale: Registration provides a simple route to extend the descriptive aspects of Land Use activities and code lists without changing the basic metalanguage elements; additions to LU_LandUseFunctionalElement subtypes are treated as additions, not changes.

nodes.label: Register for extension of the metalanguage
nodes.rationale: ISO 19144-4 defines the structure of the register but not its contents; each national body or organization sets up its own register instance so national systems can be perfectly described, while cross-system comparison rests on the standardized common elements plus registered extensions.

nodes.label: Register of legend classes (ISO 19144-1)
nodes.rationale: Distinguished from the metalanguage extension register: it records legend classes produced from a classification system, at a different level.

nodes.label: Backward compatibility through registration
nodes.rationale: Because a primary purpose of LUML is comparison between classification systems, vocabulary changes must be controlled and backward compatible: no metalanguage object may be deleted, objects may only gain attributes, and altered sub-objects are replaced by new ones with the old kept as deprecated, per ISO 19135-1.

nodes.label: LU_LandCoverLandUseRelationship
nodes.rationale: A collection class composing Land Use functional elements with Land Cover elements in a horizontal pattern, with functionalElementRelationship (default primary), optional temporalRelationship and timeLength.

nodes.label: TC211 Review Summary report (2019) recommending ISO 19144-3 and -4
nodes.rationale: A 2018 Stage 0 preliminary study on integrating specific Land Cover classifications with ISO 19144-2 and on addressing Land Use led to revising 19144-2 and creating 19144-3 (LUML) and 19144-4 (registration).

nodes.label: Revision of the ISO 19144 series (Annex C)
nodes.rationale: Aggregating and fusing data from multiple sources with different collection criteria requires a stable high-level metalanguage for both Land Cover and Land Use; all changes were kept fully backward compatible.

nodes.label: LC_GrazedCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Renamed in ISO 19144-2 to make clear that only the Land Cover effect of grazing is Land Cover; the activity itself is Land Use.

nodes.label: LC_BuiltUpSurface
nodes.rationale: Simplified in ISO 19144-2 by removing LC_Road, LC_Railway, LC_CommunicationAndOther; these become LC_LinearSurface with LC_LinearSurfaceType, with Land Use given via LUML.
